how many requests marked closed were ver.question: How many requests marked closed were verified fixed?

how many requests marked closed were ver.name: query_metric
how many requests marked closed were ver.sql:
with grouped as (
    select
        sum(case when (NOT COALESCE(outcome_group, '') IN ('neutral', 'handed_off')) and (outcome_group = 'fixed') then n_requests else 0 end) as numerator,
        sum(case when (NOT COALESCE(outcome_group, '') IN ('neutral', 'handed_off')) then n_requests else 0 end) as denominator
    from mart_outcomes_monthly
    where ("is_closed" in (?)) and (created_month between ? and ?) and (era = 'current')
)
select *, numerator / nullif(denominator, 0) as value_
from grouped

answer.answer_markdown: Among closed requests in the current system (created March 2025 to July 2026), **1,282,411 of 1,813,376** were verified fixed, or **70.7%**. The other **530,965** were closed without a code saying the work was done. That figure is `closed_unverified`. Those requests may or may not have been fixed. The data just doesn't record it.

key_numbers.label: Share of closed requests verified fixed

caveats: Current era only: legacy data has no resolution codes, so it can't show verified fixes.

Closed requests here exclude duplicates, information-only closes and intake handoffs, which are outside the fix-rate base. Many generic closures, especially in street services, mean 'not recorded as fixed', not 'not fixed'.

rows.rationale: claude-haiku-5-5: The code says the item was not set out for collection, which matches the schema's not_found meaning that the item wasn't there to act on, so the crew did no pickup. It could be read as unable, since the resident's failure to set the item out prevents the work, but the code's own words point to the item being absent. answer.answer_markdown: Three codes carry most of the gap. From March 2025 to July 2026, **530,965** requests were closed without a code saying the work was done. **QC-Item Not Out** accounts for **317,748** of them, **C-Closed** for **105,644**, and **1004-Closed** for **52,198**. Next come `1003-Referral to External Department` (**14,957**), `IWO-Issued Work Orders to Resolve` (**6,042**) and `MNT-Maintenance to Be Performed` (**4,624**). QC-Item Not Out is coded `not_found`: the item wasn't put out for pickup. That can be a legitimate outcome, so it isn't necessarily a failure. C-Closed and 1004-Closed are generic codes, so they say "not recorded as fixed", not "not fixed".

key_numbers.label: Total closed without a fix code

caveats: Current era only, requests created March 2025 to July 2026; the legacy system has no resolution codes.
I give counts, not percentage shares, because no metric reports each code's share of the gap.

answer.answer_markdown: Resident-reported graffiti requests closed **more slowly** after the relaunch. which council districts have the biggest.question: Which council districts have the biggest gap between closed and fixed?

which council districts have the biggest.name: query_metric
which council districts have the biggest.sql:
with grouped as (
    select
        "cd" as cd,
        sum(case when (NOT COALESCE(outcome_group, '') IN ('neutral', 'handed_off')) then case when is_closed then 1 else 0 end else 0 end) as a_numerator,
        sum(case when (NOT COALESCE(outcome_group, '') IN ('neutral', 'handed_off')) then 1 else 0 end) as a_denominator,
        sum(case when (NOT COALESCE(outcome_group, '') IN ('neutral', 'handed_off')) and (outcome_group = 'fixed') then 1 else 0 end) as b_numerator,
        sum(case when (NOT COALESCE(outcome_group, '') IN ('neutral', 'handed_off')) then 1 else 0 end) as b_denominator
    from fct_current_requests
    where (created_month between ? and ?)
    group by cd
),
valued as (
    select *, round((a_numerator / nullif(a_denominator, 0) - b_numerator / nullif(b_denominator, 0)) * 100, 4) as value_
    from grouped
)
select *
from valued
order by value_ desc nulls last, cd

answer.answer_markdown: Among council districts, **District 13** has the largest gap between closed and verified fixed at **30.8 points**. It is followed by **District 6 (29.3)**, **District 4 (29.1)** and **District 2 (28.4)**. The smallest gaps are **District 8 (19.6)** and **District 1 (20.5)**. The gap is the share of all requests in the base that were marked closed without a code saying the work was done. The figures cover requests created March 2025 to July 2026. Requests with no district have a gap of **36.0 points**, but that group is small (7,227 requests).
caveats: Current system only (March 2025 to July 2026). The old system has no resolution codes.
A gap reflects how requests were coded, not proof that work wasn't done. Many street-services categories close with a generic code, so the mix of categories in a district matters.
District 1 closes far fewer requests (64.6%) than the others, which is part of why its gap is smaller.
